content:
Kira Volkov: heads up: perf-canary gates for the hardware profile pack are *way* too noisy right now. getting red builds w/ no code changes. false positives are slowing down ENG-4828 + making it hard to trust regressions vs runner variance.

Kira Volkov: examples from today: same commit, re-run passes. p95 latency gate trips on H100-streaming in us-east runners, but tokens/sec stable. looks like variance + occasional long-tail outliers.

PerfCanaryBot: Build #118203 ❌ perf-canary/regression
- Gate: h100.chat.streaming.p95_ms (threshold: +2.0%)
- Observed: +3.4% (baseline 312ms → 323ms)
- Notes: n=3 runs, 1 outlier run

Sahana Iyer: +1, seeing similar on L40S runners too (INT-8832 vibes). some of the runners are underprovisioned CPU and it shows up as tail latency spikes.

Aisha Bello: can you link the dashboard slice? i want to see if it correlates with node type / region.

Kira Volkov: yep: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/perf-canary/profiles?var=gpu=H100&var=test=h100.chat.streaming (internal)
Kira Volkov: you’ll see p95 jump w/ no change in p50, and host_cpu_throttle spikes on the same runs.

Allison Grant: if CPU throttle is the driver, we should not gate on a metric that’s contaminated by runner health. can we add a precheck and mark run “invalid” when host signals are bad?

Rina Kobayashi: +1. the workload matrix runner is currently single-sampling some scenarios (n=3 total, but 1 run can dominate p95). we can bump to n=5 and use median-of-runs.

Claire Dubois: also, for the profile pack, our “baseline” for comparison is last green on main, right? if runner pool changes underneath, the baseline drifts and everything looks like a regression.

Kira Volkov: baseline is last 7 days rolling median (per gate). which is good in theory but bad if the runner pool changes or we have a noisy week.

Marcus Reed: what’s the goal of the gate? catch real regressions from scheduler/kernels. those typically move multiple metrics together (tokens/sec, p50, p95, retries). can we require 2/3 signals to fail before we block?

Aisha Bello: we can do that, but we need to be careful not to miss “tail-only” regressions (we literally had one last week w/ prefill fairness). but we could require tail regression to persist across multiple consecutive runs.

Sofia Ivanova: tail-only regressions do happen, but they are not “single outlier run” events. if it’s one run with cpu throttle, that’s noise.

Hiro Tanaka: kernels side: microbench regressions show as throughput drop pretty consistently. tail jitter is usually runtime scheduling + host. i’m ok loosening p95 gates if we keep tokens/sec + GPU util strict.

Benji Okafor: +1. can also incorporate the new profile-selection metrics we added in PR-22027 to ensure the run actually used the intended profile. we’ve had a couple “gate failed” where it was default profile due to detection mismatch.

Kira Volkov: yes pls. i’ve seen “override_source=env” in some canary runs when it should be fleet default.

Aisha Bello: proposal (v1):
1) change p95 gate from +2% to +5% for streaming tests *only*
2) require 2 consecutive failing builds OR 2/3 runs failing within a build
3) add runner-health invalidation: if host_cpu_throttle > X or perf_canary_runner_load > Y, mark run as flaky and don’t count for gating

Allison Grant: +1 on invalidation, but we need an audit trail so it doesn’t become “everything invalid”. log “invalid_reason” and page infra if invalid rate > threshold.

Irene Choi: if we’re invalidating on host signals, please route invalid-rate alerts to eng-infra too. we can fix the runners, but we need to know.

Sahana Iyer: for L40S, we should probably separate “runner health” from “product health”. right now those are conflated. i can add a pre-step that checks cpu quota + noisy neighbor signals.

Claire Dubois: also suggest shifting from absolute % delta on p95 to a confidence interval / bootstrap? i know it’s heavier, but at least something like “only fail if delta > 5% AND p-value < 0.05”.

Kira Volkov: bootstrap would be nice but might be overkill for now. if we can just do more samples per scenario, CI shrinks.

Rina Kobayashi: increasing samples increases runtime. but we can do targeted: for tail metrics (p95), run n=7 on the 3 most important scenarios; keep n=3 elsewhere.

Marcus Reed: which scenarios are “most important” for profile rollouts? i’d vote:
- h100.chat.streaming (mid context)
- h100.chat.nonstreaming (long prefill)
- l40s.chat.longctx (OOM / kv budget)

Sofia Ivanova: +1. plus one “high concurrency short prompts” scenario to catch batching regressions.

Aisha Bello: ok. i can encode that in perf-canary config (PR-731 follow-up). we can tag scenarios with `gate_tier=critical`.

PerfCanaryBot: Build #118211 ❌ perf-canary/regression
- Gate: h100.chat.streaming.p95_ms
- Observed: +2.9%
- Runner health: host_cpu_throttle=0.37

Kira Volkov: lol, perfect example. throttle is through the roof.

Allison Grant: can we define “invalid”: host_cpu_throttle > 0.15 OR cpu_iowait > 0.10 OR runner_mem_pressure == true? (numbers tbd)

Irene Choi: careful w/ cpu_iowait thresholds; some nodes have periodic spikes. but overall direction is right.

Benji Okafor: another idea: A/B within same job. run baseline build + candidate build on the *same* runner back-to-back, compare ratio. that cancels a lot of node variance.

Kira Volkov: that’s the gold standard, but doubles runtime cost. could we do A/B only for critical gates?

Aisha Bello: we can. maybe:
- critical tier: A/B on same runner (baseline artifact pinned)
- noncritical tier: compare to rolling median

Rina Kobayashi: baseline artifact pinned means we need to pick a baseline per runtime branch. should be doable though.

Claire Dubois: and we should pin prompts/datasets (we already do) + pin tokenizer version. there was that one weird drift when tokenizer got bumped.

Sahana Iyer: i’ll confirm runner images haven’t drifted. i suspect a recent kernel update on the runner AMI. will check with infra.

Irene Choi: we did roll a minor AMI update in a subset of perf runners last week (security patches). might explain the baseline drift. sorry. we can freeze the perf runner pool during the profile pack rollout if needed.

Kira Volkov: no worries, this is exactly why the gate logic needs to be robust.

Hiro Tanaka: can we also shift the gate metric from raw p95 to “p95 excluding first request after warmup”? some of the tail comes from cold-ish cache and scheduler ramp.

Sofia Ivanova: we already do warmup but it’s short. if runner is noisy, warmup doesn’t help. but for legit regressions, it’ll still show.

Marcus Reed: what do we want as policy?
- For profile changes: prefer sensitivity (catch regressions)
- For unrelated PRs: prefer specificity (don’t block)
Maybe we only enable strict gates on “profile-affecting” labels?

Kira Volkov: tricky. people change “unrelated” code and accidentally touch defaults. but we can do something like: strict gates only when profile pack is enabled in the canary build OR when touching runtime/scheduling/kernels dirs.

Aisha Bello: i’d rather keep consistent gates but add the invalidation + consecutive failures requirement. should reduce noise without needing path-based heuristics.

Allison Grant: +1. also add a “warn-only” tier. we can post to #eng-runtime but not fail CI unless it persists.

PerfCanaryBot: (reaction :thumbsup: from Aisha Bello)

Kira Volkov: action items:
- Aisha: draft change to gate logic: consecutive fail requirement + scenario tiers + loosen streaming p95 to +5% (critical only stays tight?)
- Sahana/Irene: runner health signal + invalidation criteria + alerting for invalid rate
- Rina/Claire: propose which scenarios get higher n, and what n we can afford
- Benji: sanity check we always emit selected profile + override_source in canary; if missing, treat as invalid

Aisha Bello: yup. i’ll open a PR in perf-canary today and link here.

Sahana Iyer: i’ll add runner health precheck + export `invalid_reason`. will loop in INT-8832 thread too.

Irene Choi: i’ll pause further AMI changes to perf runners until we stabilize this. will post in #eng-infra.

Kira Volkov: thank you. goal is “catch real regressions from profile changes” not “randomly block main 2x/day”.

Aisha Bello: PR incoming: relax + add consecutive fail + invalidation hooks. ETA end of day.
